results.title: Gendered Language: Dr. Deborah Tannen - LDS Dimension
results.content: In 1990, Dr. Deborah Tannen came out with an interesting and useful research-based book, You Just Don’t Understand: Women and Men in Conversation. As a researcher and an author, she shares several useful ideas in her book regarding the main differences between how men and women primarily communicate. \*We have different language styles as men and women. According to Tannen, females engage in "rapport-talk" — a communication style meant to promote social affiliation and emotional connection. After learning about and understanding these differences better, a good rule of thumb is to share with your partner that you want to just be listened to (rapport talk), or figure out the best way to address the situation (report talk) whenever the need arises. I suggest thinking of language in the 2 basic ways shared by Deborah Tannen: rapport talk and report talk. Both men and women do both styles, with men most often doing report talk and women most often doing rapport talk.
